 Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 12.03.2019 passed by 4th Addl. District Judge and Sessions Judge, Hassan, District sitting at Channarayapatna (for short 'the tribunal') in MVC.No.955/2018.

entities.text: 4th Addl. District Judge and Sessions Judge, Hassan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequate and meager compensation awarded by the NC: 2024:KHC:15013 tribunal.
Hence, the appellants seek enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under; One Sri.Krishnegowda, was traveling on his Hero Honda bike bearing Registration No.KA.05.E.5636 and unfortunately met with an accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the KSRTC bus bearing Registration No.KA.13.F.2246 on 17.03.2018.
The said Sri.Krishnegowda, was traveling along with pillion rider Sri.Rangegowda, who died on the spot.
The claimants are none other than the wife/widow of the deceased and two children of the Krishnegowda.
The claimants filed the claim petition seeking compensation for the sudden and unfortunate death of Krishnegowda.

On service of notice, Respondent-Corporation filed statement of objections, denying the claim of the claimant and age, avocation, income and the negligence Mythri vs Divisional Controller, Ksrtc on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122004904/
2 attributed against the driver of the offending Bus and also pleaded that the claimant Nos.2 and 3 are the major/adults, who are not entitled to compensation as they are not dependant on the deceased.
Hence, he sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3.2. On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
3.3. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P10.
On the other hand, respondents got examined himself as RW.1, and did not produce any documents.

On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.12,55,000/- with interest @ 9% p.a and directed respondent-corporation to pay within a period of 30 days.
3.5. Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimants are before this Court challenging the impugned judgment and award.

4. The main contention of the learned counsel for appellants-claimants is that, the tribunal has committed an error in awarding meager compensation, which calls for interference at the hands of this Court.
Accordingly, claimants seeks enhancement of compensation.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent- Corporation submits that the tribunal has rightly awarded NC: 2024:KHC:15013 just and reasonable compensation, which does not call for interference.
Therefore, on these grounds, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel for the respondent - Corporation/Insurance Company and perused the impugned judgment and award and the documents at Exs.P1 to P10.
As per the police records at Exs.P1 to P6 depict, the FIR and Charge sheet are laid against the driver of the Bus.
Hence, negligence is rightly attributed against the driver of the offending Bus.
7. Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation, income and the appropriate multiplier for awarding compensation.

It is seen that the deceased Sri.Krishnegowda, was aged about 47 years as on the date of occurrence of accident and the appropriate multiplier would be '13' which is correctly taken by the tribunal, it does not call for interference.
Tribunal has added future NC: 2024:KHC:15013 prospects of 25%, by taking the notional income at Rs.10,000/- p.m.

It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for the appellants that the income taken by the tribunal is on the lower side and the Notional Income Chart prescribes Rs.12,500/- p.m as the income.
Accepting the contention of the learned counsel, income is taken at Rs.12,500/- p.m.
The tribunal has deducted 50% towards personal and living expenses, whereas the deceased was married, survived by his wife and 2 children, who are the appellants/claimants before the tribunal.
Hence, 1/3rd would have to be deducted towards personal and living expenses rather than 50%.

Therefore, taking all these facts into consideration, the loss of dependency in this case would be Rs.16,25,052/- (Rs.12,500/- + 25%
Mythri vs Divisional Controller, Ksrtc on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122004904/
3 = Rs.15,625/- - 5208 = Rs.10,417/- x 12 x 13) Rs.16,25,052/- as against Rs.9,75,000/-.
8. I am in agreement with the learned counsel for the appellants.

The income taken by the Tribunal is on the NC: 2024:KHC:15013 lower side as the Legal Services Authority for the year, 2018 prescribes Rs.12,500/- per month and so also the deduction of 50% is erroneous and 1/3rd would have to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
9. Learned counsel for the respondent/corporation contends that the tribunal has committed an error in awarding Rs.2,15,000/- towards consortium to the claimants 1 to 3 which is highly exorbitant.

As contemplated in the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680 would be awarded and in view of this Court enhancing the compensation, the consortium amount awarded exorbitant could be reduced.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The submission made by learned counsel for the respondent/Corporation is accepted.

Towards loss of consortium, the tribunal has awarded Rs.40,000/- for the first appellant and Rs.40,000/- for the appellant Nos.1 and 3, whereas, each of the claimants would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- per person in consonance to the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi case.
Therefore, in all they would be entitled to Rs.1,20,000/- (Rs.40,000 x 3) with a 20% escalation for 2 block periods.
Therefore, the claimants are entitled to Rs.1,44,000/- under this head as against Rs. 2,50,000/- awarded under the heads consortium by the tribunal.

11. Towards loss of estate Rs.15,000/- and towards funeral expenses of Rs.15,000/- is awarded, with an escalation of 10% which is additional Rs.3,000/- is added which comes to Rs.33,000/-
(Rs.30,000/- + 10%) under this head.

In view of the above discussion, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.18,02,052/- as against Rs.12,55,000/- as mentioned in the table below:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Loss of dependency 16,25,052-00 Loss of consortium 1,20,000-00 (+ 20% escalation) 24,000-00 Loss of estate and 33,000-00 transportation of dead body,
funeral expenses.
(+ 10% escalation)
